All 45 members of [[Bexley London Borough Council]] were up for election. The election took place alongside [[2026 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]].{{Cite web |last=Coughlan |first=Joe |date=2025-04-30 |title=London local elections, why they aren't in 2025 and when the next ones will be |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/uk-world-news/london-local-elections-arent-any-31429137 |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=My London}}{{Cite web |title=Local authority, combined authority, and county combined authority election cycles in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=GOV.UK}} The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] maintained control of the council, having held control since [[2006 Bexley London Borough Council election|2006]], losing four seats. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] remained the largest opposition party despite losing three seats, and [[Reform UK]] won its first seven seats. == History == [[File:Bexley UK local election 2022 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2022 election]] The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police, and fire.{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Bexley has generally been controlled by the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] since its creation, except for the elections of 1964, 1971 and 2002 which resulted in [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] councils, and the 1994 council election which resulted in no overall control. In the 2022 election, the Conservatives won 33 seats with 50.8% of the vote across Bexley, whilst Labour won 10 seats with 44.0% of the vote. === Council term === [[Daniel Francis (politician)|Daniel Francis]], sitting Labour councillor for [[Belvedere (ward)|Belvedere]], was elected to the [[Bexleyheath and Crayford|Bexleyheath and Crayford constituency]] at the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]].{{cite news |title=Bexleyheath and Crayford - General election results 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/uk/constituencies/E14001089 |access-date=5 July 2024 |work=BBC News}}{{cite web |date=22 May 2024 |title=Bexleyheath and Crayford Labour Party candidate selected |url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/24338692.bexleyheath-crayford-labour-party-candidate-selected/ |access-date=5 July 2024 |website=News Shopper}} The resulting by-election saw Labour hold the seat with a reduced vote share.{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Belvedere Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/19358/#2024-10-17 |access-date=3 December 2024 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk}} In November 2025, the Conservatives selected councillor David Leaf to be the new council leader. The previous leader [[Teresa O'Neill, Baroness O'Neill of Bexley]] had served as council leader for 17 years from 2008 to 2025, when she announced her decision to stand down to focus on her work in the [[House of Lords]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bexley.gov.uk/news/new-leadership-london-borough-bexley|title=New leadership for the London Borough of Bexley|website=bexley.gov.uk|accessdate=15 November 2025}} During the term, two Conservative councillors leave and sit as independents: Felix Di Netimah for [[Crayford (ward)|Crayford]], and Nigel Betts for [[Falconwood and Welling (ward)|Falconwood and Welling]]. James Hunt, councillor for [[Blackfen and Lamorbey (ward)|Blackfen and Lamorbey]], left the Conservatives after they didn't select him to stand again, saying they "had lost its way both in Parliament and in Bexley." He joined Reform UK but sat as an independent on Bexley Council, and will contest the 2026 elections again as an independent.{{Cite web |date=2026-03-12 |title=‘I joined Reform — but I’d rather stand in local elections as an independent’ |url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/bexley-and-bromley/news/i-joined-reform-but-i-d-rather-stand-in-local-elections-a-337646/ |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=Kent Online |language=en}} During the [[2025 Kent County Council election|2025 Kent County Council elections]], all six seats in neighbouring [[Dartford]] were won by Reform UK on 41% of the vote, with the Conservatives losing all four of their seats and dropping from 53% to 30% of the vote; and Labour losing their single seat and dropping from 31% of the vote to 18%.{{Cite web |title=Election Results |url=https://www.kent.gov.uk/about-the-council/how-the-council-works/kent-county-council-elections/election-results |access-date=2 May 2025 |website=Kent County Council}} == Campaign == David Leaf, the new leader of the majority Conservative group on the council, attacked the [[Starmer ministry|Labour government]] saying the council has faced "brutal cuts" and that they were "forced to put council tax up" by 4.99%.{{Cite web |title=Council’s 2025/26 balanced budget is passed {{!}} London Borough of Bexley |url=https://www.bexley.gov.uk/news/councils-202526-balanced-budget-passed |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=www.bexley.gov.uk}} Leaf said "what's important for us is investing in the services that matter to our residents - whether it's supporting the thousands of residents who are elderly who benefit from social care, the hundreds of vulnerable children we protect and keep safe every day, or investing in ensuring our streets are clean."{{Cite web |date=2026-04-09 |title=Reform UK disrupt Labour/Conservative battles in Bexley |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5yx4e42prpo |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}} Stefano Borella, leader of the opposition Labour group, focused on the "50,000 renters in Bexley" and defending the government's [[Renters' Rights Act 2025|Renters' Rights Act]]. He said that Bexley needed more affordable housing, more council housing, and more investment in roads and pavements. In the House of Commons, the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024-intake]] [[Bexleyheath and Crayford]] Labour MP [[Daniel Francis (politician)|Daniel Francis]] stated that he wanted to ensure the £895,000 of government-funded pothole repair is well spent, including on Mayplace Road East in [[Barnehurst]].{{Cite web |title=Engagements - Hansard - UK Parliament |url=https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2025-10-22/debates/7D09717C-6AE9-4E42-9A79-E0295C2C555A/Engagementshighlight=bexley+council |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=hansard.parliament.uk |language=en}} Reform UK launched its London election campaign on 29 March, with party leader [[Nigel Farage]] saying "we are seriously competitive in Croydon, in Bromley, in Bexley, in Havering, and maybe two or three others."{{Cite web |date=2026-03-29 |title=Reform UK launches London election campaign in Croydon |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9vly297yk1o |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}} On 8 April, Farage campaigned in [[Welling]].{{Cite web |last=Blackshaw |first=Cameron |date=2026-04-10 |title=Farage says Reform has 'real chance' of winning Bromley and Bexley |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/south-london-news/nigel-farage-reform-real-chance-33746616 |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=My London |language=en}} Reform candidate Miles Jones said the party would cut wasteful spending, save money, fix potholes, and conduct a "real audit of council finances". However, some compare a potential Reform administration in Bexley to [[Kent County Council]], which Reform took majority control of in 2025 including winning all six seats in neighbouring [[Dartford]], promising not to raise tax but then raising it by 3.99% at their first budget.{{Cite news |last=Quinn |first=Ben |last2=correspondent |first2=Ben Quinn Political |date=2026-02-13 |title=Reform UK’s Kent council faces ‘extreme risk’ after passing first budget |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/feb/13/reform-uk-kent-council-extreme-risk-pass-first-budget |access-date=2026-04-28 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} Nigel Farage previously led [[UK Independence Party|UKIP]], which won 3 seats on Bexley Council in 2014. === Polling === {| class="wikitable sortable mw-datatable" style="text-align:center; line-height:14px;" |- ! rowspan="4" | Dates

Bexley, as is the case all other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years, with the previous election having taken place in 2022. The election takes place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors will have as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected. All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over are entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, are entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Voting in-person at polling stations takes place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters are able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election. == Candidates == This election is set to break numerous records. 192 candidates will be standing across 17 wards to compete for 45 seats. This is 71% higher than the 112 candidates standing in the 2022 election. Taking into account the changes in Bexley Council's size over the years, this election will see the highest number of candidates per seats available ever, having 4.27 candidates per seats compared to the second highest [[2010 Bexley London Borough Council election|2010]] which had 3.38 candidates per seat (213 candidates for 63 seats). Three parties are standing in all 45 seats up for election: the Conservatives, Labour, and [[Reform UK]]. This will be the 16th time for the Conservatives, who have stood candidates for every seat in every election except [[1964 Bexley London Borough Council election|1964]]; the 17th time for Labour, who have stood candidates for every seat in every election if you include a [[Labour and Co-operative Party|Labour and Co-operative]] candidate in [[1986 Bexley London Borough Council election|1986]]{{cite web |title=London Borough Council Elections |url=https://londondatastore-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/LBCE_1964-5-7.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223003753/https://londondatastore-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/LBCE_1964-5-7.pdf |archive-date=23 February 2015 |access-date=29 March 2015 |website=London Datastore |publisher=London County Council}}; and the first time for Reform UK, who stood for the first time in 2022 with four candidates. Reform UK will be the first third party to stand the maximum number of candidates since [[1994 Bexley London Borough Council election|1994]] when the Liberal Democrats stood a full house.{{Cite web |last=Blackshaw |first=Cameron |date=2026-04-15 |title=Bexley local election candidates 2026 - full list |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/south-london-news/bexley-local-election-candidates-2026-33769465 |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=My London |language=en}} The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)]] are standing 28 candidates (in 62.2% of seats), their highest number since [[2010 Bexley London Borough Council election|2010]] when they stood 40 candidates (in 63.5% of seats). The [[Green Party of England and Wales]] are standing 24 candidates (in 53.3% of seats), their highest number ever, beating their previous record of 7 candidates (in 11.1% of seats) in [[2014 Bexley London Borough Council election|2014]]. Five separate political parties (Conservatives, Labour, Reform, Liberal Democrats, and the Greens) will be standing at least one candidate in every ward for the first time, and standing in over half of the available seats for the first time.{{Cite web |date=8 May 2010 |title=Bexley |url=http://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/elections2010/boroughs/bexley/default.htm |access-date=9 May 2010 |publisher=London Councils}} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}{{Cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project - 2014 - Bexley |url=http://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/results/2014/21/ |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk}} ==Previous council composition== {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2022 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election ! colspan="3" | After 2026 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
